question.:question/problem: Let $a=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}$. Find a unit vector that is parallel to $a+3b$ and points the same direction.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u &= \frac{a+3b}{|a+3b|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}a+3b &= \begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+3\cdot \begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}9 \\ -6\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}-1+(9) \\ 0+(-6)\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|a+3b| &= \sqrt{(8)^2+(-6)^2} \\
&= \sqrt{100} \\
&= 10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $a+3b$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u &= \frac{a+3b}{|a+3b|} \\
&= \frac{1}{10}\cdot (a+3b) \\
&= \frac{1}{10}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -6\end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix}\frac{4}{5} \\ - \frac{3}{5}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

original_record.:question/problem: Let $a=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 8\end{bmatrix}.$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $2a+b$ and points the same direction.
original_record.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{2a+b}{|2a+b|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}2a+b & =2\cdot \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 8\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 8\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0+5 \\ 4+8\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 12\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|2a+b| & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{12}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{169} \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $2a+b$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{2a+b}{|2a+b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{13}(2a+b) \\  & =\frac{1}{13}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 12\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{5}{13} \\ \frac{12}{13}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
